title: International experiences of genomic newborn screening: Lessons from over 10,800 newborns.
journal: American Journal of Human Genetics 113(10):2025-2033, Oct 2026 (PMID 42767216). Europe PMC pubType 'Review'. isOpenAccess=N, inPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, so abstract only. Crossref lists a CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 VOR licence, but the only full-text route is the Elsevier API/publisher site, which I did not use.
data_url: None for this review: no data statement, deposit or supplement was found. The nearest open summary tables come from the underlying studies: Early Check Supplementary Table 1 (screen positives) and Tables 2-3 (gene-condition lists) at static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41591-025-03945-8/MediaObjects/41591_2025_3945_MOESM3_ESM.xlsx and _MOESM4_ESM.xlsx. A related ICoNS gene-inclusion table is at github.com/tjminten/gim_genelist.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: For the review: Europe PMC core record (no full text, no suppl, no text-mined accessions). NCBI elink from PMID 42767216 to gds/sra/bioproject returned nothing; elink to gap from the 3 study PMIDs returned nothing. Zenodo, DataCite and Figshare DOI searches found 0 relevant hits. I opened the Early Check S1 xlsx: 51 screen-positive rows (47 Panel 1, 4 Panel 2) with gene, transcript, HGVS, zygosity, ACMG class and clinician interpretation. G6PD has 23 rows and MITF 12. I also opened Early Check S2/S3 (178 + 29 gene-condition pairs with ASQM scores) and the ICoNS repo files: input_machinelearning.csv has 114,140 rows (gene x program), and Data_Repository.xlsx has 4,390 genes x 61 columns with per-program inclusion flags.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Review abstract: 4 gNBS studies, >10,800 newborns (US, Belgium, Australia), screen-positive rate 1.6-3.7%, G6PD the most common finding, outcome definitions inconsistent across studies. Data statements read from PMC full text: BabyScreen+ individual data are in 'controlled-access data storage at MCRI', on request (14 ClinVar SCVs, Extended Data Tables). BabyDetect: on request via an ethics committee, and its Zenodo record is pipeline code plus a demo dataset only. Early Check: on request, IRB-approved, within 12 months. I did not retrieve the GUARDIAN (JAMA 2025) data-sharing statement.

a1_downloadable.note: Fails. The review deposits no data. Individual-level data for all four studies are controlled access or on request: BabyScreen+ is in MCRI controlled-access storage, BabyDetect and Early Check need an emailed request plus ethics/IRB approval, and the GUARDIAN statement was not retrieved. Only small per-study supplementary summary tables are open.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Fails. The review has no table. Per-gene or per-condition yield would have to be built by merging four studies' supplements, which use different gene panels (169-605 genes), condition sets and outcome definitions. The abstract itself says these are inconsistent.

a3_inputs_present.note: Early Check S1 does give HGVS variants for the 51 positives (checked in the file). But no genotypes or features exist for the ~10,700 screen-negative newborns, so there are no inputs for the negative class.

a4_units_stated.note: Mostly not applicable. The open tables are categorical (gene, ACMG class, zygosity, confirmation status) or integer expert scores (ASQM 0-3), so units aren't an issue.

a5_enough_rows.note: Fails. The open labelled rows I counted are 51 Early Check screen positives. At 1.6-3.7% of ~10,800 newborns, positives across all four studies are low hundreds at most (an estimate from the abstract, not counted). That is far below 400.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <1 MB for the open screen-positive tables; 7.8 MB for the ICoNS csv

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Minor mismatch: the Early Check abstract says 50 screen positives and '28 (55%)' true positives, but S1 lists 51 numbered results. Probably one newborn had two results, but the file doesn't say. The review's per-study counts could not be checked without full text.

a8_label_provenance.note: A 'screen positive' is a lab's ACMG P/LP call within a panel, made by rules that use population frequency and in-silico evidence, so it is not an independent measurement. For the salvage ICoNS table, the label (gene included by a program) is a policy choice. Its features include ASQM actionability scores and an expert-survey '% recommend inclusion' column, both of which programs used to choose their genes. That is leakage by construction.

existing_models.name: ICoNS boosted-trees gene-inclusion model (Minten et al., Genet Med 2025, PMID 40357684; Scharfe and Boemer are co-authors)
existing_models.score_and_split: AUC 0.915 and R2 80% on a random 80/20 split of 114,140 gene x program instances. The same gene appears in both train and test across programs, so the split is leaky.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Features are expert-curated and missing for poorly characterised genes, which biases against rare or under-studied disorders. The ranked list may be overfit. They propose finding not-yet-included genes via a knowledge graph (PrimeKG).

existing_models.name: Metabolomics + genome sequencing ML for screen-positive triage (Xie et al., BMC Med Genomics 2025, PMID 41257776)
existing_models.score_and_split: 119 California NBS screen positives across 4 disorders. Metabolomics ML: 100% sensitivity; GS cut false positives by 98.8%. This is a different task (MS/MS triage, not gNBS).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: False-positive reduction varies by condition, and GS alone lacks sensitivity.

backbone.name: None fits. The open data are gene-level tabular or categorical tables, and no ESM-2/DNA-LM freeze-and-head task follows from them.
backbone.licence: Review VOR is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (per Crossref). Early Check supplements follow Nature Medicine OA terms. The ICoNS GitHub repo has no licence file (GitHub API license=null).

integration.join_key: HGNC gene symbol (present in Early Check and ICoNS tables)

controls.positive_control: Not applicable (rejected). In the salvage ICoNS table, RUSP core genes should rank at the top.
controls.negative_control: Not applicable (rejected). Salvage: shuffle inclusion labels within program.
controls.external_validation: Not applicable (rejected). Salvage: hold out whole programs (26 available).

honest_claim_h3: Any model from these open tables would claim to predict which genes research gNBS programs (mostly high-income, mostly European-ancestry cohorts) chose to screen, or which ~51-250 lab-called P/LP findings were returned. It would not predict which newborns are truly affected.
ml_idea: None viable on this review. Salvage (a separate candidate): re-evaluate the open ICoNS boosted-trees model with leave-one-program-out and leave-gene-out splits, with and without the expert-survey and ASQM features, to measure how much of AUC 0.915 is leakage. That is cheap and informative either way, but the label is policy, not biology.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Done: searched for deposited data (none) and counted the open labelled rows (51 Early Check screen positives). Individual data for all four studies are controlled access or on request.

verdict_reason: Controlled access: this is a review with no deposited data, and individual-level gNBS data for the four studies are on request (BabyScreen+ is in MCRI controlled-access storage; BabyDetect and Early Check need ethics/IRB-approved requests), so A1 fails. The only open tables are tiny per-study supplements (51 Early Check screen positives), so A5 fails. A per-gene yield label would have to be built across inconsistent study definitions (A2), and screen-positive calls are rule-based ACMG classifications (A8).
